hadith:
Ablutions (Wudu') - Narrated Ja`far bin `Amr bin Umaiya:

My father said, "I saw Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) taking a piece of (cooked) mutton from the shoulder region and then he was called for prayer. He put his knife down and prayed without repeating ablution."
message: Allah is the Lord of all worlds who sustains us with mercy and provision—Al Muqeet, the Sustainer, ensures that every living being receives what they need to survive and flourish. Just as the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) maintained his connection to Allah through prayer regardless of worldly concerns, we too should prioritize our spiritual obligations and trust in Allah's care and support. Let this remind us that true nourishment comes not only from physical provision but from our constant remembrance and submission to the One who sustains all creation.
name:
Al Muqeet - المُقيِت - The Sustainer

The name Al Muqeet comes from the Arabic root 'q-t', which relates to provision and sustenance. It reflects Allah's capacity to care for and nourish all beings, ensuring they receive what they need to survive and thrive, both physically and spiritually. This name emphasizes divine mercy and support.
verse:
Al-Fatihah - The Opener - 1:2-4

All praise is for Allah—Lord of all worlds, the Most Beneficent, Most Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgment.
